source.title: File:Battle Scene with Elephants Siam vs Burma Painting.png

ObjectName.value: Battle Scene with Elephants Siam vs Burma Painting

Categories.value: Author died more than 70 years ago public domain images|Rifles of Thailand|Elephants in art of Thailand|Armour of Thailand|Pole weapons of Thailand|CC-PD-Mark|PD-old missing SDC copyright status|Shields in Thailand|Burmese-Siamese wars|Elephant duel of Naresuan|Historical military uniforms of Thailand|Swords in art of Thailand|Military people of Thailand in art

ImageDescription.value:
Unofficial title: Battle Scene with Elephants Siam vs Burma Painting. The original painting title is unknown. The painting depicts a historical event.

Description: this is a battle scene with Siamese and Burmese officers and soldiers mounted on elephants while soldiers on the ground are firing rifles. The elephant at the center left uses its large, white tusk to pierce the neck of the center-right elephant with its front feet lifted off the ground. The high status of the men riding the elephants is evident by the white, multi-tiered umbrellas (chatra), the peacock feathers, and ornate headgear. The man at the center of the painting with an elaborate, ornate helmet is a Burmese prince (5-tiered umbrella). The figure opposite to him (center-left) is a Siamese crown prince or viceroy (7-tiered umbrella) of his army with a pointed black hat and seated under a 7-tiered umbrella. The battle would have taken place several centuries earlier during the Ayutthaya era. The painting, which dates from the late 19th century, incorporates historical aspects of the practice of warfare during the Ayutthaya period (1351–1767). Few paintings or textiles survive from the period, the clothing worn at court and by soldiers was described by European visitors and in regional historical chronicles. The painting commemorates an important moment in Siamese history.

The painting has a signature in the lower right corner: ไทวิจารณ์ (Thai Wicharn). This could be a pseudonym of an artist who was active in the late 19th century.

Geography: Thailand (Place of Origin). This is a painting detail. Measurement: 91.5 cm (height) x 109 cm (width). Made by an anonymous Thai artist, late 19th (Rattanakosin). Provenance: Doris Duke Charitable Foundation's Southeast Asian Art Collection; given to Walters Art Museum, 2002. Accession Number: 35.229.

Artist.value: Thai Wicharn (ไทวิจารณ์)

ImageDescription.value:
Contemporary painting of the Battle of Puebla, fought in Mexico on 5 May 1862 (from which the Cinco de Mayo celebrations originate) between the forces of the French Empire and the Mexican Republic. In this battle, the French army, which was invading Mexico in order to overthrow its liberal republican government and install a monarchy friendly to their own interests, was defeated by a smaller force of the Mexican army.

A text at the bottom-left corner of the painting reads "A derecha la batalla ga[na]da a los france[se]s el 5 de mayo de [18]62. Garita de Am[ozoc]" (To the right, the battle which was won against the French on 5 May 1862. Garita of Amozoc).
